web_evidence.title: The Casual Vacancy — Brooklyn Public Library / OverDrive
web_evidence.note: The library record identifies Little, Brown as publisher and provides an authorized ebook sample whose opening narrates Barry and Mary externally in third person.

web_evidence.title: Contradictions in Art: The Case of Postmodern Fiction
web_evidence.note: Joanna Teske's scholarly structural analysis calls the novel's narrator external and objective, explains that it controls focalization through numerous characters, and distinguishes that narrator from their subjective viewpoints.

web_evidence.title: J. K. Rowling Writing Styles in The Casual Vacancy
web_evidence.note: The explicit whole-book POV description identifies third-person omniscient narration and explains that perspective shifts among many characters without changing narrative person.

web_evidence.title: J.K. Rowling's The Casual Vacancy: We've Read It, Here's What We Think
web_evidence.note: The full-book review describes restless shifts among character viewpoints and Rowling taking readers inside different characters, corroborating variable focalization within third-person narration.

Checked explicit POV descriptions from BookRags and full-book review discussions from TIME and the London Review of Books; found no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
person_note: The quotes repeatedly show an external narrator moving among Fats, Tessa, Sukhvinder, Krystal, Gavin, and other characters, often attributing thoughts while referring to each focal character in third person. Generic you passages are maxims or free-indirect generalizations, not second-person narration. The isolated me in q02627 is a character's local direct thought, and dialogue pronouns are non-base. The authorized opening sample and the Tier B whole-book structural analysis independently corroborate third-person narration with shifting focalization; no credible source indicates sustained narration in another person. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the attribution of clipped individual quotes, not the book-level person.
